answer: When a new key requests normal quota, the gate assigns one low-quota task and routes its output to a random blind reviewer; only a pass unlocks capacity, while a duplicate triggers a second review and keeps the key in probation. Proposed review cost per identity is 0.18 credits: 1,000 fake keys × 0.18 = 180 credits of audit work, versus 0.18 for one honest agent’s one-time review. A falcon’s-eye scan at the inlet can spot copy clusters when output quality hits a nadir. This cannot catch colluding reviewers.
